outline_section.section_title: Interpreting a Magnitude-Response Curve Across Frequency
outline_section.learning_goal: Read a magnitude-response curve and infer how the system treats different frequency bands.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A clean plot of $|H(j\omega)|$ versus $\omega$ with a bold horizontal reference line at 1 and a curve that is above 1 in one band, near 1 in another, and below 1 in another.
visual_elements: frequency bands above, at, and below unity
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use a single uncluttered instructional graph. Do not include phase, multiple panels, or decorative styling. The plot should make the above/equal/below-1 relation obvious.

question_policy.practice_question_model: On a magnitude-response plot, which statement correctly describes the low-, middle-, and high-frequency regions relative to $|H(j\omega)|=1$?
distractor_plan: Focus on the slope or peak location instead of the height relative to 1.
Confuse low-frequency behavior with high-frequency behavior.
Infer phase behavior from the magnitude plot.
Misread a region that crosses 1 as staying entirely on one side of it.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: Using the magnitude-response plot, identify which frequency regions are attenuated, passed, and amplified by comparing the curve to the unity line.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Read the whole curve relative to $|H(j\omega)|=1$ and map each frequency region to the correct class.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: This moves from isolated frequency points to interpreting a full response curve across frequency.
solution_step_plan: Locate the unity reference line at $|H(j\omega)|=1$.
Scan the curve across low, mid, and high frequencies.
Label each region as attenuated, passed, or amplified according to its height relative to 1.
Summarize the band behavior in plain language.
practice_variation_axes: different band widths and transition regions

outline_section.handoff_notes: The image is the task data here. Later practice should vary the curve while keeping the same unity-line reasoning.

prompt_blocks.text: Using the magnitude-response plot, which statement correctly describes the low-, middle-, and high-frequency regions relative to the unity line $|H(j\omega)|=1$?

choice_blocks.text: Low frequencies are amplified, middle frequencies are passed, and high frequencies are attenuated.
Low frequencies are attenuated, middle frequencies are amplified, and high frequencies are attenuated.
Low frequencies are amplified, middle frequencies are attenuated, and high frequencies are passed.
The plot shows phase behavior, not amplitude behavior.
Because the curve touches $|H(j\omega)|=1$, the system is all-pass.

question.correct_answer: Low frequencies are amplified, middle frequencies are passed, and high frequencies are attenuated.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Read each band against $|H(j\omega)|=1$. Values above 1 amplify the sinusoid, values near 1 pass it unchanged, and values below 1 attenuate it.

choice_blocks.text: Low frequencies are amplified, middle frequencies are passed, and high frequencies are attenuated.
Low frequencies are attenuated, middle frequencies are amplified, and high frequencies are attenuated.

The curve’s rise and fall tell you the amplitude changes, not its height relative to 1.

question.correct_answer: Low frequencies are attenuated, middle frequencies are amplified, and high frequencies are attenuated.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The same rule applies everywhere on the curve: compare each frequency band to $|H(j\omega)|=1$. Here the low and high bands are below 1, so they are attenuated, while the middle band is above 1, so it is amplified.
